title: Catch an unsafe authority calculator
brief: Write verification expectations that expose control-authority bugs. The plotted candidate deliberately uses the wrong opposing-moment sign.
supplied: Which tests distinguish a correct pitch-authority calculator from a wrong opposing-moment sign, linear speed scaling, or input acceptance bug?
M_available=0.5*rho*V²*S*c*dCm; M_required=Iy*target-other; margin=M_available-M_required; initial acceleration=(M_available+other)/Iy at full command.
900 kg trainer; rho=1.20 kg/m³; V=20 m/s; S=27.25 m²; c=4 m; usable dCm=0.153; Iy=5000 kg m²; other=-750 N m; target=0.12 rad/s². Nose-up moment is positive about the declared CG.
Numerical verification cases, speed ratio, boundary rejection and insufficient-authority detection.
All reference cases use the same sign convention and compatible reference dimensions. Cases intentionally probe independent implementation errors.
Initial pitch calculation at the declared condition. Constant coefficients and inertia. No proof of successful takeoff, ground clearance, stall recovery, or safe landing.
A baseline-only test is inadequate. Zero usable coefficient must leave a negative margin when positive control demand remains.
Baseline required=1350 N m; capacity=4002.48 N m. M_available(40)/M_available(20)=4. At dCm=0, margin=-1350 N m.
Show why each test matters and identify malformed inputs separately from physically insufficient but valid cases.
Run the supplied correct and faulty candidate equations over zero coefficient, lower speed, sign reversal, and invalid inertia. No aircraft flight is simulated.
Accept only an implementation that preserves sign conventions, quadratic scaling, units, and input validation; a valid negative margin is a result, not a crash.

fields.label: Expected required moment with other=-750 (N m)
fields.help: Calculate required elevator moment for other = −750 N m. This expected value will test whether the calculator handles the opposing sign correctly. Enter a number only.

fields.label: Expected available(40 m/s)/available(20 m/s)
fields.help: Predict capacity at 40 m/s divided by capacity at 20 m/s, with all other inputs fixed. Enter a number only.

fields.label: Expected margin when usable dCm=0 (N m)
fields.help: Calculate available minus required moment when usable dCm is zero but the response requirement is unchanged. Keep the sign. Enter a number only.

fields.label: Expected behavior for Iy=0
fields.help: Iy=0 is outside this model. Choose what the software should do instead of dividing by zero.

fields.label: What should the calculator do with a valid negative margin?
fields.help: All inputs are valid, but available moment is smaller than required moment. Should the software report that result or reject the input?

fields.label: Explain your answer
fields.help: For each test, explain the mistake it is meant to catch. Distinguish a valid negative margin from an input the calculator cannot use.

checks.message: This catches adding other with the wrong sign.
This catches replacing V² with V.
Zero authority cannot satisfy a positive control demand.
A finite positive inertia is required for the response model.
An insufficient but valid condition must remain inspectable.

hints: Do not lose the minus sign in Iy*target-other.
The zero-coefficient test should produce a finite negative margin, not a runtime error.
Use separate tests for numerical correctness, insufficient margin, and malformed input.

sweep.units: Other signed moment in N m; required control moment in N m. Configured curve is deliberately faulty.

experience.scenario: A supplied calculator contains a deliberate opposing-moment sign bug. Other candidate faults include linear speed scaling and invalid-input handling.
experience.task: Enter expected results for the supplied tests. You are designing a verification table, not writing test code in this mission.
experience.method: A test needs an input, an expected result and a reason it catches a defect. A valid negative margin means insufficient authority; it is not a malformed input. A test specification can pass while correctly detecting a faulty calculator.
experience.investigate: Inspect the sign, speed-scaling, zero-authority and invalid-inertia test cases. State which defect each exposes.
experience.tools: Only this app and its calculation pad are needed.

reflection.included: The test cases check selected sign conventions, speed scaling, zero authority and invalid input handling.
reflection.omitted: Passing these examples does not prove that every possible input is handled correctly.
reflection.question: Propose one additional test input and explain what error it could reveal that the existing cases might miss.
reflection.help: Use one specific detail from this investigation. Explain what you would check next and why it matters; you do not need to perform that new test here.

experience.terms: An expected result is the answer a correct calculation should give for a chosen input. A failed software test means its output disagrees. A negative aircraft margin can be a correct software output.
